body: I think I can take a look for this issue!

Here is my finding, I think it's a little hard to be fixed.

#### For Conclusion
Currently, ```CleartextHttp2ServerUpgradeHandler``` cannot work well with ```Http2Codec```.

#### How CleartextHttp2ServerUpgradeHandler Works
```CleartextHttp2ServerUpgradeHandler``` will peek the first 24 bytes to see that it's HTTP2 preface or not, and then it will remove it from the pipeline so that the inbound bytes will forward to the handler after ```CleartextHttp2ServerUpgradeHandler```.

#### What happened when using Http2Codec with CleartextHttp2ServerUpgradeHandler
##### When channel initialized
The ```CleartextHttp2ServerUpgradeHandler``` will add ```PriorKnowledgeHandler``` into the pipeline and remove itself from pipeline.
```
+---------------------------------- Pipeline ---------------------------+
| +------+         +------------------------+                 +------+  |
| | Head |  -->    | PriorKnowledgeHandler  | -->  ..... ->   | Tail |  |
| +------+         +------------------------+                 +------+  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
And ```PriorKnowledgeHandler``` will start to **peek** (will not consume) the inbound, and determine the protocol and configure pipeline when it knows about the protocol.

##### When detect HTTP2 connection preface
When ```PriorKnowledgeHandler``` found HTTP2 connection preface, it will add handlers for HTTP2 and remove itself. After ```PriorKnowledgeHandler``` was removed, the inbound will forward to **The handler after PriorKnowledgeHandler** <- This is the point.

Here is the steps what handler added/removed.
1. [PriorKnowledgeHandler] Replace PriorKnowledgeHandler with Http2Codec
2. [Http2Codec] Add Http2FrameCodec before itself
3. [Http2FrameCodec] Add Http2ConnectionHandler before itself
4. [Http2Codec] Add Http2MultiplexCodec before itself
5. [Http2Codec] Remove itself
6. And other stuff

After that, the pipeline will look like
```
(H) -> Head
(T) -> Tail
+---------------------------------- Pipeline -------------------+
| +---+        +-----------------------+                  +---+ |
| | H |  -->  | Http2ConnectionHandler | -->  ..... -->   | T | |
| ----+        +-----------------------+                  +---+ |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
Outside pipeline
+------------------------+    +------------+             +---+
| PriorKnowledgeHandler | --> | Http2Codec | --> ... --> | T |
+------------------------+    +------------+             +---+
```
So we can see the inbound bytes was forward to orphan handlers, not forward to Http2ConnectionHandler.

#### Solution or Workaround
Currently, I don't have any idea about solution or workaround, but will keep think about it.
Are you saying that the inbound bytes are getting forwarded to `Http2Codec`, even though it has been removed from the pipeline?

It sounds like there's a much deeper design issue here. Why does Netty allow a Handler to pass an event via its `ChannelHandlerContext` when that Handler is no longer present in the pipeline and therefore does not have a defined position in that pipeline? After all, the `ChannelHandlerContext` represents a Handler's association with a pipeline--shouldn't it throw an `IllegalStateException` as soon as you try to do this?

And as for the various HTTP2 pipeline components, do they really need to rely on pipeline mutation so heavily? Your root cause analysis seems like a great example of how complex mutation-oriented programming can be *even in a single-threaded context*.

As for a fix, can `PriorKnowledgeHandler` add `Http2Codec` after itself (instead of calling `replace`), propagate the data down the pipeline, and *then* remove itself from the pipeline?

issue.title: Configures HTTP2 pipeline with more proper way

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Motivation:

When we use pipeline.replace and we still had ongoing inbound, then
there will be some problem that inbound message would go to wrong
handlers. So we add handler first, and remove self after add, so that
the next handler will be the correct one.

Modifications:

Uses remove after addAfter instead of replace.

Result:

Fixed #6881

body: @rschmitt - I address a PR to fix this issue! PTAL
@normanmaurer Can you provide any insight as to whether this may represent a bug in `replace` and/or the behavior of a `ChannelHandlerContext` after it has been removed from a pipeline?

@rschmitt sorry I am quite busy atm... Generally speaking I would love to change the contract to throw an `IllegalStateException` if someone tries to do operations after the handler was removed from the pipeline. That said I think this may break user-code and so is a breaking change so it can not be done in a non major release :/

Right, it would have to be done as an opt-in change. Maybe something like:

1. Define a system property (`io.netty.channel.ChannelHandlerContext.enforcePipelineMembership` or something)
2. Throw an `IllegalStateException` when the above property is set
3. When the above property is not set, log an error the first time this illegal state is detected
4. Run all of Netty's tests with the `enforcePipelineMembership` property set to ensure that this bug isn't hiding anywhere else in Netty's codebase
5. Document that passing events to a removed context has undefined behavior and will be made illegal in a future release

issue.title: Use addAfter in Http2Codec.handlerAdded(....) to ensure we not end up…

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
… with incorrect handler order

Motivation:

When pipeline.replace(...) is used with the Http2Codec we will end up with an incorrect pipeline view for the handler that was replaced because the Http2Codec will add handler in front of itselv but the handler that will be replaced thinks that the Http2Codec is the handler that will be "next" in the pipeline.

Modifications:

- Use addAfter(...) in Http2Codec.handlerAdded(....) and so ensure correct ordering.
- Port tests written by @chhsiao90 in [#6952] to verify the fix.

Result:

Fixes [#6881]


If there is no issue then describe the changes introduced by this PR.
